zephzoid 09/30/26 Boiling your rice the right way for five minutes can strip out nearly three quarters of its arsenic. A University of Sheffield team boiled rice in extra water for five minutes, then drained and finished cooking it fresh. That step removed 73 percent of inorganic arsenic from white rice and 54 percent from brown. Rice absorbs far more arsenic than other grains because it grows in flooded fields. Skip the mystery grain, find local grain farmers on Localize. Sources: University of Sheffield 706 197 71 349
